title: Import reconciliation B0: pure exact-scope hold decision over the journal view
outcome: One pure function decides, from child A's import-reconciliation journal state and one dispatch candidate's exact scope, whether the candidate is held by import reconciliation, admitted, or unknown. It is a foundation for B's admission and handoff gates, with no production caller and no behaviour change.
acceptance: A new module holds one pure function. It reads child A's journal state and one dispatch candidate's exact scope: store association, project id, original binding and the current host incarnation. It returns one typed disposition: HeldByImportReconciliation, naming every covering fence record in journal key order; Admitted; or Unknown, naming its reason. It takes no lock, does no I/O or persistence, and has no production caller.

Table-driven tests with deterministic fixtures show: NotActivated gives Admitted. An activated journal with no fence gives Admitted. A covering fence gives Held in every phase, including Reconciled with a terminal decision ref, because only removing the record releases the guard. A covering fence from another host incarnation stays Held. Two covering fences give Held naming both. A sibling in another project, or under another store association, gives Admitted. Under a fence scoped to one owner, a candidate resolved to a different owner with complete coverage gives Admitted, and under an owner-scoped covering fence, an Unknown or Legacy binding, an owner that cannot be resolved, an owner whose coverage is unknown, and a journal whose state cannot be established (child A's typed load refusal) each give Unknown, while a whole-scope covering fence gives HeldByImportReconciliation for any candidate in its scope, including an unbound one.
No dispatch behaviour changes, on never-activated hosts or anywhere else, and the full gate passes on the exact committed tree. This slice claims none of w-9e40's own acceptance criteria.
